name: Viña Senior Residences
award: 2024 Federal 9% (Round One) and 4% housing tax credits (paired)
headline: Columbia Ventures is building Viña Senior Residences, a six-story, 152-unit building for seniors 62 and older at 30% to 60% AMI, with an 8,000 sq ft senior center on the ground floor, at 2150 E. 49th Ave. in Denver's Elyria-Swansea neighborhood. It is financed by a 50-unit 9% award from CHFA's 2024 Round One and a 102-unit 4% bond award, and Denver issued its building permit in August 2025.
why_it_matters: It is a 'twinned' 9% and 4% deal in one building split into two condominiums, with CHFA as bond issuer and volume cap provider, Denver linkage fee loans on both sides and a Denver Housing Authority partnership for the property tax exemption.

status.label: Under construction: Denver building permit issued 2025-08-07; placed in service targeted Q2 2027
status.detail: Denver's permit data show a foundation and excavation permit issued 2025-07-08 and a new-building permit for 152 units (valuation $20,219,551, contractor I-Kota) issued 2025-08-07, plus a further permit issued 2026-03-06. Denver City Council approved both city loans on 2025-06-16. Columbia Ventures targets placed in service in Q2 2027; no certificate of occupancy was found.

next_step: Watch Denver's permit data for a certificate of occupancy at 2150 E. 49th Ave. and CHFA's placed-in-service records for both condominiums.

background.text: How the pieces fit: one 152-unit building is split into two condominiums, mostly by vertical stacks of units. The competitive 9% award funds 50 units and the bond-backed 4% award funds 102; sharing the core, shell and infrastructure is the applicant's main cost-containment argument.

Master plan: it is phase two of the 6.2-acre 48th and Race site next to the National Western Center. Phase one, the 150-unit Viña Apartments with the Tepeyac clinic and retail, was completed in April 2022. Urban Land Conservancy bought, remediated and rezoned the land (with City Council hearings in 2015 and 2016 on a land acquisition loan and rezoning), and a Columbia Ventures subsidiary bought the phase two site in June 2023.

Community process: six community meetings in 2018 led to a Community Benefits Agreement, and Columbia Ventures holds quarterly community meetings; the January 2024 meeting covered the senior building. The developer plans to notify Elyria-Swansea residents of openings first and to extend local hiring.

The concept changed before the application: in March 2023 the developer described 150 to 180 units at 30% to 70% AMI, with groundbreaking targeted for Q3 2024 and completion in 2026; the 2024 application set 152 units at 30% to 60% AMI and a closing by May 2025.

Denver's loans: City Council's housing committee approved both loan resolutions by consent on 2025-06-04 and full Council adopted them on 2025-06-16. Each requires a covenant recorded against the property for at least 60 years. The 4% side's restrictions are 6 units at 30% AMI (5 one-bedroom, 1 two-bedroom) and 96 at 60% AMI; the 9% side's are 5 at 30%, 5 at 40%, 26 at 50% and 14 at 60%.

The market study flagged 40%, 50% and 60% AMI penetration rates above CHFA's preferred thresholds; the applicant answered with 98% occupancy and waitlists at comparable senior properties and a 17.4% overall capture rate. The Phase I reports found no recognized environmental conditions on or next to the parcel.
